LESSON: WRITING 3.4.1 ELEMENTS OF EFFECTIVE WRITING

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 3
Topic 3.4: Writing 3.4.1 Elements of effective writing
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 4

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Writing 3.4.1 Elements of effective writing, part of Strand 3 in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10 ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: Why should we organise ideas logically in writing?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. explain the use of addition, similarity and contrast connectors in a text,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Writing 3.4.1 Elements of effective writing in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. explain the use of addition, similarity and contrast connectors in a text,

   Writing 3.4.1 Elements of effective writing helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. identify connectors of addition, similarity and contrast from a text. Learners with speech difficulties could be 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. identify connectors of addition, similarity and contrast from a text. Learners with speech difficulties could be 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Writing 3.4.1 Elements of effective writing together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Self-efficacy as the learner exhibits concerted attention to detail as they use pictorials to sequentially order events from

a narrative.

● Problem Solving as the learner follows instructions very carefully as they are guided to collaborate and rearrange

disordered sentences from word cards to form a logical paragraph.

Values:
● Unity is promoted as the learner appreciates the importance of oneness as they team up to write a coherent paragraph

on a topic around the theme.

● Respect is enhanced as the learner exercises positive regard for self and others as they collaborate and rearrange

disordered sentences from word cards to form a logical paragraph.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Citizenship education as learners manifest principles of leadership as they team up to write a coherent paragraph on a topic

around the theme.

Suggested Learning Resources: Dictionaries, newspapers, charts and realia, resource persons, audio recording, adapted

digital devices with filter keys/key guards/larger mouse/head control input devices such as head wand. universal

cuffs/wrist braces/arm braces, weighted pencil/pen grips
